does: Fries coarse bulgur in fat with softened onion and a spoon of paste until every grain is coated, then covers it with hot liquid and leaves it under a lid, without stirring, until the grains have swollen, drunk the liquid and stand apart.
how: Soften the onion in the fat, then stir in the pepper or tomato paste and fry it until the colour deepens.
Add the bulgur and stir for a short while until each grain is coated and smells toasty.
Pour in hot water or stock, a little more than the volume of the bulgur, and add salt. Bring it to a boil.
Cover and turn the heat to its lowest. Do not stir.
When the liquid has gone, take the pan off the heat, lay a cloth under the lid and leave it to stand.
Fluff the grains with a fork before serving.

cues.text: Small steam holes show in the surface and no liquid is left in the pan.
The grains are plump and tender with a slight bite, and they fall apart when fluffed.
A nutty, savoury taste with the sweetness of the onion and paste.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring while it cooks, which breaks the grains and turns them sticky.
mistakes.fix: Stir only when the grains are coated, and fluff at the end.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in too much liquid, which leaves a wet porridge.
mistakes.fix: Measure the liquid and use only a little more than the bulgur.

mistakes.mistake: Serving it straight from the heat, so that it is wet and clumped.
mistakes.fix: Let it stand under a cloth and lid first.

comes_after.why: The onion is softened in the fat before the grain goes in.

variant_of.differs: The grain is coarse bulgur, which is already steamed and dried, so it needs no washing or soaking and takes less liquid and less time than rice. A spoon of pepper or tomato paste goes in with the onion for colour and body.
